title: Derived tensor cohomology of modules is naturally Tor
statement: For any commutative ring R, let B_n(M,N)=H^n(single_0(M) tensor^L single_0(N)), with maps induced by the derived tensor in each variable [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. For every integer k, the bifunctor B_{-k} is naturally isomorphic to Tor_k(M,N) when k is nonnegative, and to the constant zero bifunctor when k<0 [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Naturality holds simultaneously in both module variables, without flatness or finite generation assumptions.

source.place: Stacks Project Algebra Tags 00LY and 00LZ; More on Algebra Tag 0H7Z, identification of tensor cohomology with Tor

proof.text: Extend a projective resolution of M by zero to cochain degrees at most zero. Projective terms are flat and the complex is bounded above, hence K-flat. Its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Use the K-flat tensor comparison and the single-complex tensor comparison to identify single_0(M) tensor^L single_0(N) with the image of the extended termwise tensor complex.

Apply the ordinary derived cohomology comparison, the map-extend comparison and extend-homology comparison. ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj identifies degree -k with the kth left derived tensor, which is Tor. Prove naturality of the K-flat comparison using the lax monoidal structural map and quotient comparison. Resolution lifts commute with the augmentation and compute the first-variable Tor map; the tensoring-right natural transformation commutes with extension and computes the second-variable map. Compose these equations into an isomorphism of bifunctors.

For k<0, derived tensor of the two degree-zero modules is bounded above by zero. Therefore its positive cohomology is zero; use the canonical isomorphism to zero, whose naturality follows from uniqueness of maps to zero. This also covers zero objects and the zero ring.
